item.title: Splitting of projective modules over some affine algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.13984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article focuses on defining the Euler class group of stably free module and analyzes the condition for existence of unimodular element in corresponding projective module.This is an improvisation of work by Banerjee and Das, On a question of Nori:Obstructions,improvements and appliaction. If A is a smooth affine algebra over certain affaine algebras.
item.dc:creator: Subarna Mandal

item.title: A lower bound on $\text{depth} \ \mathbf{A/I^n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ be an ideal in $A$. Let $\ell(I)$ be the analytic spread of $I$. Let $G_I(A) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ be the associated graded ring of $I$ and let its depth be $t$. We prove $\text{depth} \ A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Tony J. Puthenpurakal

item.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
item.description: arXiv:2610.15261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.
item.dc:creator: Manolis C. Tsakiris

item.title: On modular vector invariant fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of any characteristic and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ the general linear group over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Suppose $W$ denotes the standard representation of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ acts diagonally on the direct sum of $W$ and its dual space $W^*$. Let $G$ be any subgroup of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$. Suppose the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W)^G=\mathbb{F}_q(f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k)$, where $f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k\in\mathbb{F}_q[W]^G$ are homogeneous invariant polynomials. We prove that there exist homogeneous polynomials $\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}$ in the invariant ring $\mathbb{F}_q[W\oplus W^*]^{G}$ such that the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W\oplus W^*)^{G}$ is generated by $\{f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k,\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}\}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
item.dc:creator: Ying Han, Runxuan Zhang

item.title: Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domains with non-Pr\"ufer integral closure
item.description: arXiv:2610.15444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There exists a one-dimensional local Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domain whose integral closure is not Pr\"ufer. We prove that the recently constructed coherent counterexample to the normalization problem has this stronger Gorenstein property. The argument establishes permanence of divisoriality of finitely generated ideals under ultraproducts and quotients by divided primes. It also supplies uniform matrix factorizations: in an ultraproduct of plane-curve domains, every nonzero ideal generated by $r$ elements is a cycle of a two-periodic totally acyclic complex with free terms of rank $r$. The divided prime defining the one-dimensional example is flat, so these complexes descend through the quotient and localization. A specified two-generated ideal remains noninvertible in every integral overring. Over the normalization, its associated Laurent overring has nonzero first Tor with every injective cogenerator, although both rings are Gorenstein flat over the original domain. Examples distinguish this failure from a nonnormal Gorenstein curve with Pr\"ufer normalization and show that the periodicity conclusion is stronger than the Gorenstein Pr\"ufer property alone.
item.dc:creator: Hwankoo Kim

item.title: An overring characterization of Gorenstein Pr\"ufer domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.15454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a commutative integral domain is Gorenstein Pr\"ufer if and only if every overring is Gorenstein flat over the original domain. It is enough to test overrings that are finitely generated as algebras. The proof combines finite duality with a conductor-quotient argument. Under the overring hypothesis, the conductor quotient of a proper overring generated by two elements as a module is an IF-ring, and degree-one duality lifts first syzygies of finitely presented quotient modules to totally reflexive modules. This gives a bound of one for the Gorenstein flat dimension of every module annihilated elementwise by conductor powers. Quadratic integral elements provide such conductors at nonnormal localizations, while normal localizations give principal-ideal neighborhoods. Constructible compactness yields a finite cover, and a bounded complex of localizations combines these bounds over the original domain. Consequently every finitely generated ideal is Gorenstein flat and the domain is coherent. Examples distinguish finite-type from module-finite tests and Gorenstein flatness from ordinary flatness.
item.dc:creator: Hwankoo Kim

item.title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
item.description: arXiv:2610.15869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellens\"atze for free modules.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Cimpri\v{c}

item.title: On Z-Noetherian Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.16178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, introduce a new finiteness condition for commutative rings, called $Z$-Noetherian, under which every ideal contained in the set of zero-divisors $Z(R)$ is finitely generated. This condition lies properly between Noetherian and $Nil_{*}$-Noetherian. We establish intrinsic characterizations of $Z$-Noetherian rings and investigate their stability under nilpotent quotients and localizations. Under the assumption that $Z(R)$ is an ideal, we obtain a primary decomposition theorem for ideals contained in $Z(R)$. For $ZD$-rings, we prove a Cohen-type criterion characterizing $Z$-Noetherian in terms of the finite generation of prime ideals contained in $Z(R)$. We further establish $Z$-Noetherian analogues of the Hilbert Basis Theorem and Krull's Intersection Theorem. Finally, we establish a principal ideal theorem for $Z$-Noetherian rings. Collectively, these results show that several fundamental finiteness and structural properties of Noetherian rings extend to the broader class of $Z$-Noetherian rings.
item.dc:creator: Ambar Dubey, Tushar Singh, Shiv Datt Kumar

item.title: Characterizations of t-Almost Dedekind Domains via w-Secondary Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.16685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be an integral domain and let $w$ denote the $w$-operation on $R$. A nonzero GV-torsion-free $R$-module $M$ is called $w$-secondary if, for every $r\in R$, either $M/rM$ is GV-torsion or $r^nM=0$ for some $n\in\N$. A $w$-module $M$ is said to admit a $w$-secondary representation if $M=(N_1+\cdots+N_n)_w$, where each $N_i$ is a $w$-secondary submodule of $M$. Such a representation is called minimal if the ideals $P_i=\sqrt{\Ann_R(N_i)}$ are pairwise distinct, and $M$ is called $w$-representable if it admits such a representation. If the sum can be chosen direct, then $M$ is called strongly $w$-representable. We characterize $w$-secondary modules and investigate their localization and $w$-closure properties. For a nonfield domain $R$, we prove that $R$ is $t$-almost Dedekind if and only if $\wdim R=1$ and every $w$-representable $w$-module is locally strongly $w$-representable: each of its nonzero localizations at maximal $w$-ideals is strongly representable. Global strong $w$-representability is retained when all the radical annihilators in the representation are nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Hwankoo Kim, Hyungtae Baek, Haleh Hamdi

item.title: Solomon--Terao Algebras: Top Degree, Dimension, and Homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.16951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Solomon--Terao algebra and the Solomon--Terao complex of a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal A$ in $\mathbb C^\ell$. Let $\eta$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d\geq2$ whose restriction to every flat of $\mathcal A$ has no critical point away from the origin. We prove that the Solomon--Terao algebra $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,\eta)$ has top degree $|\mathcal A|+\ell(d-2)$ and a one-dimensional top graded component with an explicit generator, solving a conjecture of Abe, Maeno, Murai, and Numata. For $d=2$, we show that the total dimension of $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,\eta)$ is bounded below by that of the Orlik--Solomon algebra. Both results hold without assuming that the arrangement $\mathcal A$ is tame. Finally, we prove that $\mathcal A$ is tame if and only if all positive-degree homology groups of the Solomon--Terao complex associated with $\eta$ vanish.
item.dc:creator: Hanyu Cai, Haiyang Chen, Shixuan Zeng, Shanwei Zhang

item.title: Asymptotic Lech Bounds and Bertini Flags
item.description: arXiv:2610.17784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a \(d\)-dimensional Noetherian local ring \((R,\m)\), with \(d>0\), let \(\cinf(R)\) be the limit, as \(N\to\infty\), of the suprema of \(e_R(I)/(d!\length_R(R/I))\) over ideals \(I\) with \(\sqrt I=\m\) and \(\length_R(R/I)>N\). We prove that if \(R\) is complete, reduced, equidimensional, and Cohen--Macaulay on the punctured spectrum, with \(d\geq2\) and infinite residue field, then every nonzerodivisor \(x\in\m\) satisfies \[ \cinf(R)\leq \max\left\{\cinf(R/xR),\sup_{\fp\ne\m}e(R_{\fp})\right\}. \] As an application, we prove the asymptotic Lech conjecture of Huneke, Ma, Quy, and Smirnov in arbitrary characteristic: \(\cinf(R)=1\) whenever \(\widehat R\) has isolated singularities. This also settles the conjecture of Ma and Smirnov that the Lech--Mumford constant \(\cLM(R)\) is attained when \(\widehat R\) has isolated singularities and \(\cLM(R)>1\). For reduced equidimensional Cohen--Macaulay standard graded algebras of dimension \(\geq2\) over infinite perfect fields, we prove attainment and rationality of \(\cLM\) for the completed vertex local rings of sufficiently high Veronese subrings. In characteristic zero, a refinement of our method produces nonisolated klt affine cones in every dimension \(d\geq3\), with \(d-2\)-dimensional singular loci, whose completed vertex local rings have \(\cinf=1\) and arbitrarily large \(\cLM\).
item.dc:creator: Hong-Ge Chen, Fei Liu

item.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Liwski

item.title: Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.18346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The complete intersection forms are the homogeneous polynomials whose annihilator ideal or the Macaulay dual, is an Artinian complete intersection ideal. In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal. Further, we also compute the Waring rank of the product of binary forms in different sets of variables.
item.dc:creator: Meghana Bhat, Enrico Carlini, Shreedevi K. Masuti, Ronnie Sebastian

item.title: Improved Upper Bounds for the Rank of the Determinant Tensor via Glynn's Formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.18394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we improve the upper bound for the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ determinant tensor to $\mathcal{B}_n-2^{n-1}+n+1$ by finding a new tensor decomposition of the tensor, where $\mathcal{B}_n$ denotes the $n$-th Bell number. The main idea is to replace a part of the tensor decomposition suggested by Houston--Goucher--Johnston with a tensor that is essentially the same as the $n \times n$ permanent tensor, and to use Glynn's formula. This upper bound gives an improved upper bound for the Waring rank of the $n \times n$ determinant polynomial for $n \geq 17$ as well.
item.dc:creator: Jeong-Hoon Ju, Hayoung Choi, Taehyeong Kim

item.title: On the existence of Gorenstein injective covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.18620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category, we characterise the Gorenstein injective covering property by several equivalent conditions, including closure under coproducts. To complete this characterisation, we construct a countable commutative Noetherian Cohen--Macaulay local ring of dimension one for which this property fails, answering negatively Iacob's question Question 1 whether character modules of Gorenstein injective modules over left Noetherian rings are Gorenstein flat. Using this characterisation, we prove that for Noetherian schemes the covering property is Zariski-local. Moreover, assuming that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathrm{QCoh}(X))$ is a covering class, we establish compatible adjunctions and recollements for homotopy categories of injectives and totally acyclic injective complexes under open restriction. However, this property is not stalk-local: we construct a commutative Noetherian ring $S$ such that $\mathcal{GI}(S_{\mathfrak{p}})$ forms a covering class for all prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}$, but $\mathcal{GI}(S)$ do not form a covering class.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Hua, Shun-Jie Li, Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.14060v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices. To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Yurkov

item.title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
item.description: arXiv:2610.14083v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data. As an application, we give a series of roots for the general determinantal ideal prove the strong monodromy conjecture for them. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal variety, monodromy conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Chen, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
item.description: arXiv:2610.14417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $\gamma(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $\Lambda_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notin\Lambda_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}\omega_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $\omega_{i}$ in the ring $\Lambda_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Sebasti\'an Uribe Rinc\'on

item.title: Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.14931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction. We also introduce quasiprojective pairs of adjoint functors and prove a coherence criterion that generalises the criterion of Gomez Pardo and Martinez Hernandez to arbitrary Grothendieck categories. Finally, we extend Stenstr{\"o}m's characterisation of coherence via FP-injective modules to compactly assembled Grothendieck categories: such a category is coherently assembled if and only if the class of CM-injective objects, defined through compact morphisms, is closed under filtered colimits. Along the way we revisit the various equivalent conditions for the coherence of a ring, collecting them in a single place. The proofs make use of the compactly assembled categories of Efimov.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Dusman, Alexander Pavlov

item.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellens\"atze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Cimpri\v{c}

item.title: The $\lambda$-chain condition of a finite partially ordered set
item.description: arXiv:2610.15971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is shown that a certain finite partially ordered set arising from an algebra with straightening laws on a finite distributive lattice satisfies the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, its application to commutative algebra is briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Sora Miyashita

item.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.16350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products. As a consequence, when $g\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, $T_{n,L}$ satisfies property $(N_p)$ for $\mathrm{deg}(L)\geq(n+1)g+p$. This bound is sharp for elliptic symmetric squares and also gives evidence for a folklore conjecture on adjoint syzygies.
item.dc:creator: Wenbo Niu, Peter Yi Wei

item.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2610.17441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Daisey

item.title: Geometric and homological interpretations of tensor flattenings
item.description: arXiv:2610.17875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We relate several nonlinear flattenings of structure tensors of finite algebras and modules to their algebraic and homological invariants. Since smoothability of algebras is equivalent to their structure tensors having minimal border rank, this shows equivalence of several tensor-theoretic nonsmoothability certificates to known classical ones. Particularly, we prove two conjectures of Dole\v{z}\'alek and Micha{\l}ek relating the tangency flattening and the $3\times3$ minor flattening to dimensions of tangent spaces to the Hilbert scheme of points. In the process, we generalize the tangency flattening to a mixed regime with two tensor inputs, relating this to dimensions of $\operatorname{Ext}$ modules, and introduce the dual notion of the cotangency flattening, related to dimensions of $\operatorname{Tor}$ modules. In the case of algebras, we also realize the kernel of the dualized tangency flattening within the setting of Harrison cohomology, making the connection to the tangent space of the Hilbert scheme explicit.
item.dc:creator: Mat\v{e}j Dole\v{z}\'alek, Jakub Jagie{\l}{\l}a, Piotr Oszer, Tim Seynnaeve, Colin Stastny

item.title: On the initial Betti numbers
item.description: arXiv:1912.10864v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R$ be a Cohen-Macaulay local ring possessing a canonical module. We compare the initial and terminal Betti numbers of modules in a series of nontrivial cases. We pay special attention to the Betti numbers of the canonical module. Also, we compute $\beta_0(\omega_{\frac{R}{I}})$ in some cases, where $I$ is a product of two ideals.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: Rational invariants of even degree polynomials under the orthogonal group
item.description: arXiv:2501.17504v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we construct a generating set of rational invariants for the action of the orthogonal group $\text{O}(n)$ on the space $\mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{2d}$ of real homogeneous polynomials of even degree $2d$. This generalizes a paper which addressed the case $n=3$. The main difficult with the generalization lies in a surprising connection to the graph isomorphism problem, a classical problem of computer science.
item.dc:creator: Henri Breloer

item.title: Realizing resolutions of powers of extremal ideals
item.description: arXiv:2502.09585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extremal ideals are a class of square-free monomial ideals which dominate and determine many algebraic invariants of powers of all square-free monomial ideals. For example, the $r^{th}$ power ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ of the extremal ideal on $q$ generators has the maximum Betti numbers among the $r^{th}$ power of any square-free monomial ideal with $q$ generators. In this paper we study the combinatorial and geometric structure of the (minimal) free resolutions of powers of square-free monomial ideals via the resolutions of powers of extremal ideals. Although the end results are algebraic, this problem has a natural interpretation in terms of polytopes and discrete geometry. Our guiding conjecture is that all powers ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ of extremal ideals have resolutions supported on their Scarf simplicial complexes, and thus their resolutions are as small as possible. This conjecture is known to hold for $r \leq 2$ or $q \leq 4$. In this paper we prove the conjecture holds for $r=3$ and any $q\geq 1$ by giving a complete description of the Scarf complex of ${\mathcal{E}_q}^3$. This effectively gives us a sharp bound on the betti numbers and projective dimension of the third power of any square-free momomial ideal. For large $i$ and $q$, our bounds on the $i^{th}$ betti numbers are an exponential improvement over previously known bounds. We also describe a large number of faces of the Scarf complex of ${\mathcal{E}_q}^r$ for any $r,q \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Trung Chau, Art M. Duval, Sara Faridi, Thiago Holleben, Susan Morey, Liana M. \c{S}ega

item.title: Companion matrices, permutations and lattice ideals
item.description: arXiv:2511.06555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates a novel connection between reductions of companion matrices associated with a symmetric family of certain binomial ideals in the coordinate ring of affine n-space and permutation matrices. Specifically, for fixed monomial orders, we observe that the reduced companion matrices yield permutation matrices satisfying group-theoretic relations. We explore the implications of these reductions, their connections to lattice ideals, and characterize the groups generated by these transformations.
item.dc:creator: Nsibiet E. Udo, Praise Adeyemo

item.title: Annihilator of $Ext^g_R(R/I,R)$
item.description: arXiv:2601.20596v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the higher divisorial ideal $D(I) := Ann(Ext^g_R(R/I,R))$ associated to an ideal $I$ of grade $g$. Our main focus is the containment problem $ D(I) \subseteq \overline{I}$. We show that this inclusion holds for broad classes of ideals, including unmixed ideals of finite projective dimension over $3$-dimensional quasi-normal rings, parameter ideals in quasi-Gorenstein rings, and powers of perfect ideals under suitable homological conditions. If $R$ is Cohen--Macaulay local, $I$ is height-unmixed, and suppose $pdim_R(R/I)<\infty$, then we show $ D_R(I)=I\subseteq \overline{I}.$ Conversely, we construct explicit examples demonstrating the necessity of these hypotheses. We develop structural properties of $D(I)$, relating it to unmixed parts, reflexive closures, symbolic powers, Frobenius closure, and trace ideals. Applications include the rigidity property of homological annihilators, a criteria for the triviality of reflexive modules and vector bundles on punctured spectra, as well as new connections among annihilators of Ext, conductor ideals, and local cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideals of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.08159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate the $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideal of a graph, a natural generalization of the closed neighborhood ideal. Let $G$ be a simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $S=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring over a field $K$. For a vector $\textbf{k}=(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\in \mathbb{N}^n$ satisfying $1\leq k_i\leq \textrm{deg}_G(i)+1$ for all $i$, the $\textbf{k}$-neighborhood ideal of $G$ is defined as the squarefree monomial ideal $$\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n\, (\textbf{x}_W:\, W\subseteq N_G[i],\, |W|=k_i)$$ of $S$, where $\textbf{x}_W=\prod_{i\in W} x_i$. We study homological invariants and properties of $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ focusing on its Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, projective dimension and Cohen-Macaulayness. Special attention is devoted to the case where the vector ${\textbf{k}}$ is the degree-vector of the graph, i.e., $k_i=\textrm{deg}_G(i)$ for all vertices $i$, and to the case where $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ coincides with the edge ideal of a graph. In these settings, we provide combinatorial characterizations and bounds for the regularity and projective dimension of $\textrm{NI}_{\textbf{k}}(G)$ for several classes of graphs, and further investigate the Cohen-Macaulay property of these ideals.
item.dc:creator: Somayeh Moradi, Leila Sharifan

item.title: On complete intersection projective closures of monomial curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.15366v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the complete intersection property of projective closures of affine monomial curves. For monomial curves in the four-dimensional affine space, we give a complete characterization of when the defining ideals of their projective closures are complete intersections. We also investigate when the projective closures are arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay.
item.dc:creator: Anargyros Katsabekis

item.title: Contravariantly finite resolving subcategories over commutative local rings are trivial ones
item.description: arXiv:2608.25626v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a contravariantly finite resolving subcategory over a henselian local ring must be the subcategory of free modules or the whole module category or the subcategory of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules. This removes the Gorenstein assumption from a theorem of Takahashi. We also show that a resolving subcategory of finite type other than the subcategory of free modules must be the subcategory of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules. As a consequence, every Cohen-Macaulay local ring of finite CM type is uniformly dominant, thereby establishing a stronger form of a conjecture of Takahashi.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Mifune, Gen Tanigawa

item.title: The structure of almost symmetric almost complete intersection numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2609.24880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a structure theorem for numerical semigroups H that are almost symmetric and almost complete intersections. We show that a row-factorization (RF) matrix of H must possess a highly regular structure, which we call a cascade matrix. Consequently, the defining ideal I_H of the semigroup ring k[H] also exhibits a highly regular structure, derived from this cascade matrix. Both the RF-matrix and the binomial minimal generating set of I_H are unique. Conversely, this structure completely characterizes almost symmetric almost complete intersection numerical semigroups: to every cascade matrix M we associate a monoid H and, whenever this is a numerical semigroup, we prove that H is pseudo-symmetric, almost complete intersection, and has M as RF-matrix. As a consequence of our study, we obtain several key results. 1) Rigidty: if an almost complete intersection semigroup is almost symmetric, then it is forced to have odd embedding dimension and to be pseudo-symmetric. This result is a ``next step'' after Kunz's theorem, which states that an almost complete intersection semigroup is never symmetric. 2) Huneke-Ulrich structure: the toric ideal can be realized as the ideal of entries of an alternating matrix multiplied by a vector of variables, and this yields the licci property. 3) Cascade polynomials: for each odd positive integer e, we construct a multivariate squarefree polynomial P_e with integer coefficients, arising from a cascade matrix of variables. We provide an enumerative interpretation of its coefficients, thereby proving their non-negativity. 4) Herzog--Watanabe question: we prove that every minimal relation of an arbitrary numerical semigroup H can be obtained by subtracting two rows in some RF-matrix of H, affirmatively answering a 2019 question by Herzog and Watanabe.
item.dc:creator: Kazufumi Eto, Naoyuki Matsuoka, Alessio Moscariello, Takahiro Numata, Alessio Sammartano, Kei-ichi Watanabe

item.title: On the $b$-invariant of a normal graded ring
item.description: arXiv:2609.32003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $b$-invariant of a normal graded ring was defined recently by Okuma, Watanabe, and Yoshida. We study this for invariant rings of finite groups, proving that it is nonpositive in the case of abelian groups, but not necessarily otherwise; more generally, we give a description of the anticanonical module for invariant rings of finite groups. Turning to infinite groups, we record the anticanonical module and the $b$-invariant for families of determinantal rings. We also construct standard-graded Cohen-Macaulay rings of characteristic zero, with isolated singularities and negative $b$-invariant, that are not of strongly $F$-regular type, thereby disproving a conjecture of Okuma-Watanabe-Yoshida.
item.dc:creator: Aryaman Maithani, Anurag K. Singh, Kei-ichi Watanabe

item.title: Characteristic-free Kn\"orrer periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2609.37839v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the Kn\"orrer functor induces an equivalence ${\underline{\operatorname{MCM}}}(R) \simeq {\underline{\operatorname{MCM}}}(A)$ of stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules, where $R = S/(f)$ is a complete hypersurface ring and $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$ is the hyperbolic extension of $R$. No hypothesis is placed on the residue field or on its characteristic, $f$ need not define an isolated singularity, and $S$ need not contain a field. This is in contrast to the iterated double branched cover $R^{\sharp\sharp} = S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, which is stably equivalent to $R$ only in characteristic not equal to $2$. We also give a direct construction of a free resolution identifying $\operatorname{syz}_2^A(M)$ with the image of $M \oplus \operatorname{syz}_1^R M$ under the functor, and an example in characteristic two in which the corresponding statement for the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ fails.
item.dc:creator: Graham J. Leuschke

item.title: Stanley-Reisner Theory in Mixed Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2609.38947v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss a class of mixed characteristic rings defined analogously to Stanley-Reisner rings by replacing one variable with a uniformizing parameter for a discrete valuation ring. We adapt Hochster's formula for Tor and Ext modules, Hochster's formula for local cohomology, and Terai's criterion for Serre conditions to this new setting; one of the tools needed is cellular sheaf cohomology, for which we give a brief treatment.
item.dc:creator: Mel Hochster, Olivia Strahan

item.title: Asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of (co)homology modules involving powers of ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.05803v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian standard $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring, and let $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ be homogeneous ideals of $R$. Let $L,M$, and $N$ be finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}$-graded $R$-modules with $N\subseteq M$. For $\underline{n} :=(n_1,\dots,n_r)\in\mathbb N^r$, set ${\bf I}^{\underline{n}}:=I_1^{n_1}\cdots I_r^{n_r}$. We study the asymptotic behaviour of the (Castelnuovo-Mumford) regularity of two families of Ext and Tor modules: those obtained from the quotients ${\bf I}^{\underline{n}}M/{\bf I}^{\underline{n}}N$, and those obtained from the quotients $M/{\bf I}^{\underline{n}}N$, with $L$ as the first argument in both the families. For each fixed homological degree, we prove that the regularity of the former family is eventually given by the supremum of finitely many linear functions of $\underline{n}$, where the coefficient of $n_i$ belongs to the set of degrees of generators of $I_i$. For the second family, when at least one of the ideals $I_i$ is generated by homogeneous elements of positive degree, we establish, under suitable conditions, a dichotomy: the regularity is either eventually equal to the regularity of the Ext or Tor module of $(L,M)$, or exhibits the same asymptotic behaviour as in the first family. These results follow from a theorem describing the asymptotic behaviour of the regularity of $(U+{\bf I}^{\underline{n}}V)/{\bf I}^{\underline{n}}W$, under suitable conditions, where $U$, $V$, and $W$ are graded submodules of a finitely generated graded $R$-module with $W\subseteq V$.
item.dc:creator: Dipankar Ghosh, Ramakrishna Nanduri, Siddhartha Pramanik

item.title: On the k-th Milnor and k-th Tjurina Numbers of a Foliation
item.description: arXiv:2510.24868v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notions of the $k$-th Milnor number and the $k$-th Tjurina number for a germ of holomorphic foliation on the complex plane with an isolated singularity at the origin. We develop a detailed study of these invariants, establishing explicit formulas and relating them to other indices associated with holomorphic foliations. In particular, we obtain an explicit expression for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation and, as a consequence, a formula for the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function. We analyze their topological behavior, proving that the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant, whereas the $k$-th Tjurina number is not. In dimension two, we provide a positive answer to a conjecture posed by Hussain, Liu, Yau, and Zuo concerning a sharp lower bound for the $k$-th Tjurina number of a weighted homogeneous polynomial. We also present a counterexample to another conjecture of Hussain, Yau, and Zuo regarding the ratio between these invariants. Moreover, we establish a fundamental relation linking the $k$-th Tjurina numbers of a foliation and of an invariant curve via the G\'omez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index, and we extend Teissier's Lemma to the setting of $k$-th polar intersection numbers. In addition, we derive an upper bound for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation in terms of its $k$-th Tjurina number along balanced divisors of separatrices. Finally, for non-dicritical quasi-homogeneous foliations, we obtain a closed formula for their $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ribeiro, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez

item.title: Finite fields whose members are the sum of a potent and a 5-potent
item.description: arXiv:2512.16942v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there are only finitely many finite fields whose members are the sum of an $n$-potent element and a $5$-potent element. Combining this with the algorithmic results provided by S.D. Cohen {\it et al.}, we confirm in the affirmative the conjecture posed in \cite{Cohen} concerning all finite fields satisfying this condition. Furthermore, we obtain several elementary results related to the more general problem of decomposing every element of a finite field into the sum of an $m$-potent and an $n$-potent (as formulated in \cite{Cohen}), proving that the number of finite fields satisfying this condition is finite.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Zhou, Peter V. Danchev, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: Correlated Gaussian Moments Determine Polynomials up to Orthogonal Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2608.14475v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $P$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $m$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. We construct finitely many correlated Gaussian moments that determine $P$ up to an orthogonal change of variables. The number of copies and the rational covariance matrices are specified in terms of $d,m$. On coefficient balls, the induced map on orthogonal orbits has a H\"older continuous inverse with an explicit exponent. For $m\geq3$, the normalised local stationary-phase expansion at the critical branch through the origin equals the Gaussian moment series. Its coefficients recover the same finite moment vector, without assumptions on the other critical points. If the leading homogeneous part has an isolated complex critical point, we compute the twisted de Rham ranks and construct formal lattices on each fixed coupling support.
item.dc:creator: Obayda Julien Assaad

item.title: A codimension formula for intrinsic perturbation of $A$-hypergeometric series
item.description: arXiv:2609.22414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the canonical formal solution space of a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system in a generic direction. We present as a finite-dimensional cokernel the quotient of that space by the span of the series obtained by intrinsic perturbation, taken over all exponents occurring in that space and all ordered negative support families, and we compute the codimension of that span. We show that the presentation and the codimension transfer to the holomorphic solutions on a common nonsingular domain. We apply these results, for every integer $q\geq 1$, to a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system of lattice rank 2 with $5q$ columns. We show that the canonical formal solution space of this system has dimension $12q^2$ and that the span of the series obtained by intrinsic perturbation has codimension exactly $\lceil 3q^2/4\rceil$ in that space.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano

item.title: Ramified Quivers with Potentials, Monodromy Characters, and Cluster Bases I
item.description: arXiv:2610.09868v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct categorical models and cluster characters for skew-symmetrizable cluster algebras admitting good ramified realizations. Goodness is equivalent to nondegenerate realizability. When a reddening sequence is given, it is enough to check sign coherence of the arrow types along that sequence. Triangular extensions with arbitrary connecting bimodule types preserve goodness when both component matrices admit reddening sequences. Consequently, every matrix obtained from one vertex by triangular extensions and mutations admits a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization for every compatible positive integral symmetrizer. For a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization, the monodromy $F$-polynomials satisfy mutation for all finite decorated representations, without a rigidity hypothesis. A full initial order determines valued universal presentations and their cluster characters. Under the reachability condition, these characters form a basis of the middle cluster algebra for arbitrary geometric coefficients, with frozen variables inverted, and contain all cluster monomials. The same family is an upper-cluster-algebra basis when the middle and upper algebras coincide. For a fixed Jacobian algebra and $\delta$-vector, the Newton polytope of the generic monodromy $F$-polynomial is independent of the order.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
item.description: arXiv:2610.11013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\delta=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $(x+\delta t,y+\delta z,z,t)$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $\ZZ[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Ivan Shestakov
